Formulation
Patient presents with acute-onset dizziness and unsteadiness, associated with ear buzzing and nausea. Symptom onset was sudden while performing routine activity. No evidence of infection or neurological deficit on brief assessment. A similar, brief episode occurred a month earlier but resolved spontaneously. Medical history includes premature ovarian failure treated with HRT. Socially, lives with and supported by husband. Protective and risk factors related to mental health are not documented.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
    - Relieve dizziness and unsteadiness; return to normal functioning
- Clinical Goal(s):
    - Symptomatic control of labyrinthitis; monitor for complications or new symptoms
- Actions (Patient):
    - Take prescribed medication as instructed
    - Book and attend follow-up appointment with doctor for further examination
    - Monitor and report any new symptoms (e.g., weakness, severe headache, vomiting)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
    - Prescribe symptomatic medication (unclear medication name), one tablet three times daily for 10 days
    - Arrange follow-up in-person consultation for ear and neurological examination, blood pressure check
    - Provide safety-netting advice (attend A&E if symptoms worsen as specified)

Secondary Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
    - Ongoing management of premature ovarian failure
- Clinical Goal(s):
    - Continue monitoring for complications related to HRT and ovarian failure 
- Actions (Patient):
    - Continue HRT as prescribed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
    - Review ongoing management as required
